messages.content:
Read the following synthetic observations about everyday computer use during local language model inference. Write a practical summary comparing the workloads, explain the limits of the observations, and recommend what a user should record when sharing a benchmark. Do not invent measurements. Treat every observation as qualitative rather than evidence that one machine or setting is faster.

Observation 1.1: web browsing. The participant was connected to external power, with several reference pages and a video playing in a browser. The local model received the same saved request as in the other sessions. The participant watched tab switching and video playback while the answer was generated. No application was closed merely to improve the reported result. The notes should distinguish prompt processing from text generation and record whether the reply ended early. Any slowdown could reflect competing work, memory pressure, storage access, or ordinary run variation; this observation alone cannot identify its cause.

Observation 1.2: document editing. The participant was connected to external power, with a long report with comments and embedded images. The local model received the same saved request as in the other sessions. The participant watched typing latency and document scrolling while the answer was generated. No application was closed merely to improve the reported result. The notes should distinguish prompt processing from text generation and record whether the reply ended early. Any slowdown could reflect competing work, memory pressure, storage access, or ordinary run variation; this observation alone cannot identify its cause.
